samples.text:
Recently, more people are using artificial intelligence programs to ask advice about their personal problems, like relationship problems or feeling sad. In my opinion, this is more a negative development than a positive one.

Some people think AI advice is useful. It is available at any time, even in the middle of the night, and it is free or very cheap. Also, some people feel shy to talk about their problems with friends or family, so they prefer to type their questions to a computer because nobody will judge them. For this people, AI can be a first step to understand their feelings.

However, I believe the disadvantages are more serious. Firstly, a computer program does not really understand human emotions. It gives answers based on data, but it does not know the person's full situation, their culture or their family history. Because of this, the advice can be too general or even wrong. For example, if someone has a serious problem in their marriage, a program cannot replace a trained counsellor who listen carefully and ask the right questions.

Secondly, people may become depend on AI and stop talking to real people. Friends and family give not only advice but also love and support, which a machine cannot give. If people share their problems only with a computer, they may feel more lonely in the long term. There is also a privacy problem, because personal information is saved by the companies who make these programs.

In conclusion, although AI can give quick and easy advice, I think this trend is negative because the advice is not always reliable and people can lose the real human connection that they need when they have difficulties.
samples.why: Clear negative position · both sides considered but ideas somewhat general · paragraphing logical though linking is formulaic · adequate vocabulary · several errors in agreement, determiners and word form that do not block meaning.

samples.text:
Artificial intelligence chatbots are no longer used only for practical tasks; many people now turn to them for guidance on their relationships and emotional struggles. Although this can offer some short-term comfort, I believe it is, overall, a negative development.

It is easy to understand the appeal. AI programs are available around the clock, cost little or nothing and, crucially, do not judge. A person who feels embarrassed about a problem may find it easier to describe it to a machine than to a friend, and the response can help them organise their thoughts. For people who live in areas with few counsellors, a chatbot may be the only source of guidance available.

However, these advantages are outweighed by several serious concerns. The most important is that AI does not truly understand the people it is advising. It produces plausible answers based on patterns in data, but it cannot read body language, notice what is left unsaid or take full account of a person's history. As a result, its advice may sound convincing while being inappropriate, and in situations involving serious emotional distress this could be harmful.

A further problem is the effect on human relationships. Talking through a difficulty with a friend or relative is not only a way of finding a solution; it also strengthens the bond between them. If people increasingly confide in software instead, they may become more isolated, which is the opposite of what someone in a difficult situation need. There are also questions about how technology companies store and use such sensitive conversations.

In conclusion, while AI can be a convenient starting point for reflecting on personal issues, relying on it for emotional advice is a worrying trend. It should complement, rather than replace, support from people and qualified professionals.
samples.why: Clear negative position throughout · counter-argument acknowledged and main ideas well extended · clear progression with varied linkers · some less common vocabulary (plausible, confide) · frequent error-free sentences, occasional slip.

samples.text:
As conversational AI has become more sophisticated, a growing number of people are consulting it about matters that were once discussed only with close friends, family members or therapists. While I accept that such tools can play a modest supporting role, I regard the broader trend as a largely negative one.

The case in favour deserves to be taken seriously. Chatbots are instantly accessible, inexpensive and endlessly patient, and for someone too ashamed or anxious to confide in another person, the anonymity of a screen may lower the barrier to seeking help at all. Articulating a problem in writing can itself bring clarity, and a well-designed program may point users towards professional services they would not otherwise have considered.

Yet the limitations are fundamental rather than incidental. Personal difficulties are rarely what they first appear to be; a dispute with a partner may be rooted in years of unspoken resentment, and low mood may signal a condition requiring clinical attention. A skilled counsellor draws on tone, hesitation and context to uncover these layers, whereas an AI can only respond to the words it is given. Its answers therefore tend towards the generic, and because they are expressed fluently and confidently, users may place more trust in them than they merit.

Perhaps more troubling is what this habit may do to human connection. Seeking advice from a friend is an act of trust that deepens relationships, and receiving support reminds people that they are not alone. If individuals increasingly bring their most intimate concerns to software designed to keep them engaged, they risk becoming more isolated precisely when they most need others. Entrusting commercial platforms with such sensitive information raises additional concerns about privacy.

In conclusion, AI may usefully serve as a first step, but as a substitute for human insight and care it is inadequate. For that reason, the growing reliance on it for personal advice should be viewed with considerable caution.
samples.why: Nuanced, clearly negative judgement · opposing view fairly evaluated · ideas extended with insightful examples · seamless cohesion · sophisticated, precise vocabulary · wide range of complex structures, essentially error-free.
